task: Draft a configuration reference section for a fictional server application. Document all six supplied options with their types, defaults, and valid ranges or enum values. Include the environment-variable override pattern and the precedence rule. Use only the supplied facts; do not infer undocumented options or defaults. Target 400–600 words.

facts.text: pool_size: integer, default 10, valid range 1 to 100.
pool_timeout: integer (seconds), default 30, valid range 1 to 300.
pool_idle_timeout: integer (seconds), default 600, valid range 0 to 3600; a value of 0 disables idle timeout.
max_retries: integer, default 3, valid range 0 to 10; a value of 0 disables retries.
retry_delay: float (seconds), default 1.0, valid range 0.1 to 60.0.
log_level: string enum, valid values are debug, info, warn, and error; default is info.
All six options can be overridden by an environment variable using the prefix NEXASERVER_ followed by the uppercase option name (for example, NEXASERVER_POOL_SIZE=20).
Environment variable values override configuration file values when both are present.
The configuration file is in TOML format.
These six options are the only ones documented in the supplied packet.

forbidden_additions: An invented option not in the supplied facts.
A default or range that differs from the facts.
A precedence order other than environment variables overriding configuration file.
Omission of the zero-disables semantics for pool_idle_timeout or max_retries.
preserve: All six options with correct types, defaults, and ranges or enums.
NEXASERVER_ environment variable prefix and override precedence.
TOML format for the configuration file.
